clue.text: Exemption from keeping me held regularly

indicators.note: the word from holds the other letters within it, as if keeping them
every second letter of the words me held is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Someone claims a pass from duty because they were detained at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks E, E, D from 'me held'; 'keeping' puts them inside FROM.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom from an obligation is an exemption from it, a release from having to comply.

clue.text: Flower caught on bird

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Fal in Cornwall
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A blossom has been snagged on a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as flow-er, a river: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The falcon is a fast-flying bird of prey, used in falconry.

clue.text: Tempt European with time in French city

indicators.note: in means the letter for time goes inside the name of the French city

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone lures a fellow European to spend time on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T inside NICE, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt someone by offering something attractive.

clue.text: Despair as novel about Portugal vanishes

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the letter for Portugal
novel means new, so the letters of despair as come out in a new order

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A book about despair in Portugal disappears from sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals the rearrangement, giving DISAEARS; 'about' then wraps that round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that disappears goes out of sight, as anything that vanishes does.

clue.text: I'm right to remove leaders to get power

indicators.note: the leaders are the opening letters of the two words I'm right, which are taken away

explanation.surface: A rebel claims to be justified in toppling the leaders to seize control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove leaders' drops I and R, the first letters of 'I'm' and 'right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, as in the saying might is right.

clue.text: Send on rugby player?

definitions.meaning: to pass a letter on to a new address
a member of the pack in rugby, one of the front eight

explanation.surface: A coach decides to bring a substitute rugby player onto the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the eight players of the scrum are the forwards; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is forwarded when sent on, and the scrummaging players in rugby are called forwards.

clue.text: Got inside military shelter with English knight left behind

indicators.note: inside means the word got goes within the word for a military shelter

parts.note: a fort is a fortified military post
taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: An English knight got into an army bunker but was left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knight' gives N, the chess notation, not the usual K of the monarch's titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten is left behind, as an umbrella left on a train is.

clue.text: Rake to stir up small leaves

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for small goes out of the word for stir up

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or awaken
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A gardener uses a rake to stir up a few small leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' suggests a garden tool, but it is the debauched man; 'leaves' takes S from ROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A roué is a dissolute man given to immoral pleasures, the same as a rake in its old sense.

clue.text: Silver ring an American scratched — is Edward worried?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
O is a ring by its shape

indicators.note: scratched means the letter for American is crossed out of the word an

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward frets over a silver ring that an American has scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratched' takes A from AN, leaving N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agonised is anguished or tormented by worry, more intense than merely concerned.

clue.text: Attractive person losing last hair, upset

indicators.note: losing last means the final letter of the word for an attractive person is dropped

parts.note: a dish is informal for an attractive person
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A good-looking person is upset at losing the last of their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing last' drops H from DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to distress is to upset, cause anxiety or sorrow.

clue.text: Woodwind instruments not following stringed instruments

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for following is dropped

parts.note: flutes are woodwind instruments
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An orchestra lists which woodwind players are not following the string section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes F from FLUTES.
explanation.definitionFit: The lute is a plucked Renaissance instrument with a pear-shaped body and strings.

clue.text: Beginning to gossip with a slur — our drunk's talkative

indicators.note: the beginning of the word gossip is its first letter
drunk means the letters of a slur our stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy gossip slurs words and won't stop chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: G starts 'gossip'; 'drunk's' rearranges A SLUR OUR into ARRULOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrulous person talks too much, especially about trivia: chatty and loquacious.

clue.text: Control by foreign military craft

definitions.meaning: the holding of a country by invading troops
a trade or job, as in a craft one follows

explanation.surface: An army takes charge of a country using foreign vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like boats in the surface, but it is the trade sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A country held by an invader is under occupation, and one's trade or job is also an occupation.

clue.text: Jetty parking that is next to river

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sign by the jetty says the parking spot is the one next to the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a platform built out over water where boats can moor, much like a jetty.

clue.text: Thought about fine lesson read in church

parts.note: re is a Latin word meaning about or concerning
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
a lection is a passage of scripture read in a church service

explanation.surface: A worshipper ponders a pleasant Bible reading heard in church.
explanation.walkthrough: LECTION is a church word for a reading from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflection is a careful thought or consideration, as in reflections on life.

clue.text: However choppy neither vessel leaves island

indicators.note: choppy, like rough water, says the letters of neither vessel are churned up
leaves means the letter for island goes out of the fodder

explanation.surface: On rough water, no boat leaves the island, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes I from NEITHER VESSEL; 'choppy' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are sentence adverbs meaning in spite of that, introducing a contrast.

clue.text: Something vital from German city — it's picked up by almost everyone

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word it is lifted and read from the bottom

parts.note: the word it, its 's standing for is as a link

indicators.note: almost means the word for everyone loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A German city holds something vital that nearly everybody picks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns IT into TI, as in a down clue; 'almost' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential is a necessity, something absolutely indispensable.

clue.text: Taking off after key found on computer? It's what prisoner might be doing

indicators.note: after places the word for taking off behind the computer key

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
aping is mimicking, taking someone off

explanation.surface: An impressionist mimics someone once they find a computer key, as a jailbreaker might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' looks like departing, but it means imitating.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner breaking out of jail is getting away, so is in the act of fleeing captivity.

clue.text: Forming response, Charlie moves to the front

indicators.note: the letter for Charlie is shifted from its place up to the start of the word

parts.note: a reaction is a response
Charlie is the NATO alphabet word for C

explanation.surface: Charlie steps forward in reply as a group is being formed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves to the front' takes the C of REACTION to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation is the act of forming or bringing something into being.

clue.text: Doctor slips hurrying out of hospital unexpectedly

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of slips hurrying are altered
out of means the letter for hospital is removed from the fodder

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor trips while rushing out of the hospital without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram signal; 'out of' first takes H from SLIPS HURRYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening surprisingly is happening in a way nobody foresaw.

clue.text: Tea leaf, in the main

parts.note: tea leaf is rhyming slang for thief, and the main is the open sea, so a thief at sea

explanation.surface: A tea leaf floats, mostly, in a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea leaf is Cockney rhyming slang for thief; 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means on the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A seagoing robber who attacks ships is a thief operating on the open ocean.

clue.text: Faction to follow in cricket?

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for faction after the word in

parts.note: a sect is a faction or splinter group

explanation.surface: A group of fans turns up to watch the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' suggests the sport, but the question mark flags the chirping creature as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket is a chirping grasshopper-like creature, one example of the six-legged kind.

clue.text: Partly open a container

parts.note: a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A lid sits loosely on a container, leaving it slightly open.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open, not fully shut, the plain synonym here.

clue.text: Check pins and notice bends

indicators.note: bends means the letters of pins notice are twisted out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone examines pins and spots that they are bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bends' rearranges PINS NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspection is a careful examination, a check that all is in order.

clue.text: Criticise current Conservative anxiety

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does
I is the physics symbol for electric current
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the UK political party

explanation.surface: Critics attack the present Tory party for its worries.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear or alarm, an extreme form of anxiety.

clue.text: Pretty loud tune

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A melody played loudly is still rather nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful or good-looking, as in fair maiden: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Fake restriction needing no introduction

indicators.note: the word for restriction loses its introduction, its first letter

parts.note: a limitation is a restriction

explanation.surface: A counterfeit rule is so well known it needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' drops the L from LIMITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a copy passed off for the real thing, a fake.

clue.text: Half-baked crackers son leaves

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for son goes away from the word for crackers

parts.note: crackers is informal for mad, insane
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A boy walks off leaving some underbaked crackers behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes S from INSANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-baked idea is foolish and ill-thought-out, as is an inane one: senseless.

clue.text: Some from Brazil are negative about army officer

indicators.note: about means that run is turned round and read the other way
some of the letters from the words Brazil are negative are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A few people in Brazil are pessimistic about one of the military's top brass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some from' takes LARENEG from 'Brazil are negative'; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is among the highest ranks of officer in an army.

clue.text: Struggle to learn ahead of examination

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A student finds it hard to memorise everything before the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to learn' gives the old verb meaning to study by heart, not the swindle sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest is a fight or struggle between rivals for a prize or position.
